# Template: circuit_diagram
A rectangular electric-circuit loop built from component pictograms (resistor zigzag, battery long/short plates, bulb circled X, switch, and capacitor plates): in series every component is spliced one after another along the top wire; in parallel the loop opens 2-3 separate rungs between the top and bottom rails so each component gets its own branch. The battery always sits centered in the bottom wire regardless of where it appears in the component list. Small arrowheads along the rails show the direction of conventional current, clockwise starting from the battery's + terminal, when requested. Choose this scene for ANY request about a circuit diagram, an electric circuit, a resistor, a battery, a light bulb, a switch, a capacitor, series vs parallel circuits, or the direction of conventional current.
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "topology": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "series",
    "parallel"
   ],
   "description": "Loop topology (default \"series\")."
  },
  "components": {
   "type": "array",
   "minItems": 2,
   "maxItems": 5,
   "items": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
     "type": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
       "resistor",
       "battery",
       "bulb",
       "switch",
       "capacitor"
      ]
     },
     "label": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Caption under/beside the component (default: its type name)."
     }
    },
    "required": [
     "type"
    ]
   },
   "description": "2-5 components in the loop, in order. Exactly one battery is recommended; it is always drawn centered in the bottom wire regardless of its position in this list. The remaining components are spliced along the top wire (series) or become the parallel rungs between the rails (parallel), in list order."
  },
  "show_current": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Small arrowheads on the rails showing current direction, clockwise from the battery's + terminal (default true)."
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- wire: the rectangular loop's plain wire segments — rails, top/bottom wire, and any rung stubs (one group)
- comp_<i>: the i-th entry in `components`, as a pictogram (i = its index in the `components` array, not draw order)
- comp_label_<i>: comp_<i>'s caption
- current_<i>: a small current-direction arrowhead on a wire segment, present only when show_current
Examples:
Request: "Draw a series circuit with a battery, a bulb and a switch." → params: {"topology":"series","components":[{"type":"battery"},{"type":"bulb","label":"Lamp"},{"type":"switch"}]}
Request: "Draw two resistors in parallel with a battery." → params: {"topology":"parallel","components":[{"type":"battery"},{"type":"resistor","label":"R1"},{"type":"resistor","label":"R2"}]}

In YAML: `template: circuit_diagram` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
